# APWorld data (generated)

These files are generated by `apworld/tools/convert_db.py` from the Corruptovania database (preset "Starter Preset").
**Do not edit by hand.** They are self-contained Python data: no imports, no access to `randovania`
(SPEC 3a). Every file can be read with `import` or with `ast.literal_eval` on the value part.

**Independent of the setup (E23, T30).** No requirement assumes starting items: they are item leaves like every other
item, so the APWorld can let each slot choose its starting items. Trick leaves stay in the requirement trees and are
evaluated by the APWorld with the slot's trick levels ("Tricks" below). Every escape requirement (E18, E22) is computed
without tricks, and a location rule is only left out where it is implied for every starting inventory and every trick
setting. T30 preserved the original rules with default starting items and tricks off. T36 adds the Vaccine and
Flux Control re-entry rules described below.

## Generating

In the repo root:

```powershell
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/convert_db.py
```

Optional `--out <folder>` (default: this folder). The output is deterministic and independent of
`PYTHONHASHSEED` (test). Check:

```powershell
venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest apworld/tools/test_convert_db.py -s
```

The test `test_committed_data_is_up_to_date` fails if the checked-in files do not match the database.
The converter does not write `__init__.py` and this README. A full T36 run took 36.5 s on Windows with Python 3.12
(T30 was about 45 s and the first T36 implementation took about 115 s). The DNF solver reuses each requirement
until one of its event inputs changes and re-evaluates only dependent connections and event sources. Conjunctions
with a true operand reuse the other operand. The five generated files match the T36 handover output byte for byte.

Playthrough simulator (only on this data, without Randovania; see "node lock" and "Check matrix" below):

```powershell
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py --seeds 100 --eager 0.5
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py --seeds 100 --eager 0.5 --without "Morph Ball"
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py --seeds 100 --eager 0.5 --usable
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py --matrix
venv/Scripts/python.exe apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py --start-table
```

Sizes and load times (T30, from `.pyc`): `logic.py` 2.91 MB, 0.13 s (unchanged); `locations.py` 1.06 MB, 0.07 s
(before T30: 0.22 MB, 0.01 s); `tricks.py` 0.16 MB, 0.004 s (the APWorld only needs it for its options).

## Files

### `locations.py`

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `LOCATIONS` | list of exactly 99 locations, sorted by `id` (1–99) |
| `UNPATCHED_LOCATION` | pickup index 0 (Olympus, MedLab Delta). The patcher never touches it (E13); it is **not** an AP location and not part of the AP logic (E17). `vanilla_item` = `Hypermode` (for information only: that is what location 0 gives locally in the game) |

A location: `{"id", "name", "region", "area", "node", "category", "escape_requirement"}`, for the 71 locations with
a rule also `"escape_triggered_events"`, `"escape_assumed_events"` and `"escape_inlined_events"`.
- `id` = pickup index of the Corruptovania loader = numbering of the patcher. That is the AP location ID.
- `name` = `"<region> - <area> - <node>"`, unique. Some region names themselves contain a " - " (e.g. `SkyTown, Elysia - Main`).
- `region`/`area`/`node` address the node in `logic.REGIONS`. `category` = `major` or `minor`.
- `escape_requirement`: the location's own access rule (E22/E24). `{"and": []}` = no rule (28 locations).
- `reentry_events`: events whose post-event path is part of the location rule (91).
- `missable: "after_goal"`: after the intro, the graph reaches this location only after the goal (1 and 2).
  The APWorld marks it `EXCLUDED` so it holds only filler (E24, T38).

### `items.py`

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `ITEMS` | the AP pool: one entry per item name with `count`. Sum of all `count` = **99** (= number of locations): default pool (100) **minus one Missile Expansion** (48 instead of 49). **Hypermode is in the pool** (E17 revised) |
| `STARTING_ITEMS` | starting items according to the preset (Charge Beam, Power Beam, Combat Visor, Scan Visor, Space Jump Boots, Morph Ball, Morph Ball Bombs). The default only: no requirement assumes them (E23), the APWorld may start a slot with fewer |

An item: `{"name", "category", "location_category", "count", "progression", "progressive", "is_expansion", "unlocks_lock", "lock", "stages"}`.
- `category`: GUI category (`beam`, `missile`, `energy_tank`, `energy_cell`, `hypermode`, …).
- `stages`: list of stages, per stage a list `(resource name, amount)`. The n-th copy received gives stage n
  (the last one applies to all further copies). Not progressive = one stage. Resource names are the names used in the requirements
  (`type: "item"`). The converter leaves out Randovania's pure counter "Item Percentage".
- `progressive`: more than one stage. `Progressive Beam` = Plasma Beam, then Nova Beam. `Progressive Missile` = Ice Missile, then Seeker Missile.
- `progression`: `True` if the item gives a resource that some requirement asks for. Exception: expansions whose
  unlocking item alone already provides the highest required value (Missile Launcher gives 5, at most 5 is required;
  Ship Missile gives 3, 1 is required). These are Missile Expansion and Ship Missile Expansion (`False`).
- `lock` (launcher lock, otherwise `None`): `{"locked_by", "item", "temporary", "respects_lock", "opened_by"}`. Without the main item
  `opened_by` the ammo (`item`) only ends up in `temporary` and does not count. The main item (`unlocks_lock = True`) transfers
  the intermediate amount. `respects_lock` is on in the preset (E15: off in the AP patch, the client reproduces the lock).
  Note: in Randovania's Prime 3 data the resource `locked_by` is set by no item. So Randovania itself keeps routing expansions
  into `temporary` even after the launcher. For AP the possession logic applies: whoever has `opened_by` gets the ammo.
  The logic needs at most 5 Missiles or 1 Ship Missile, so this changes no reachability.

### `logic.py`

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `REGIONS` | `{region: {"areas": {area: {"nodes": {node: info}}}}}`. `info["type"]` is `generic`, `dock`, `pickup`, `event` or `teleporter_network`, plus `heal`. Pickup: `pickup_index`, `category`. Event: `event`. Dock: `dock_type`, `weakness`, `target`, optional `lock`. Teleporter: `network`, `is_unlocked`, `requirement_to_activate` |
| `CONNECTIONS` | list of `{"from", "to", "kind", "requirement"}` (nodes as tuple `(region, area, node)`). `kind` = `area`, `dock` or `teleporter_network`. Directed. `from` must be reached and `requirement` satisfied. Connections into the node of a dangerous event have `escape_gate` = event name. Their `requirement` is an AND of the DB requirement, `escape_requirement` and, when present, `reentry_requirement`. |
| `EVENTS` | `{event: {"kind", "sources": [{"node", "requirement"}]}}`. An event counts as reached as soon as a `node` is reachable and its `requirement` is satisfied. `kind`: `db` (event node), `dock_lock` (blast shields as `Dock Lock: <region> - <area> - <node>`), `teleporter_network` (`Teleporter Network: <network>`). Dangerous events (22) additionally have `node` (their only event node), `escape_requirement` and `escape_inlined_events`. E24 adds `reentry_requirement` and re-entry analysis fields where applicable. |
| `TEMPLATES` | `{name: requirement}`, resolved via `{"type": "template", "name": ...}` |
| `NODE_TYPES` | number of nodes per type (control) |

**Requirement tree:**
- `{"and": [...]}`, `{"or": [...]}` (empty `and` = always satisfied, empty `or` = never).
- `{"type": "template", "name"}`
- `{"type": "item"|"event"|"trick"|"damage"|"misc"|"version", "name", "amount"}` and optionally `"negate": True`.
  - `item`: amount owned ≥ `amount` (amounts from `stages`, plus starting items).
  - `event`: event in `EVENTS` reached.
  - `trick`: the slot's level for that trick ≥ `amount` (1 beginner … 5 hypermode). The level is a parameter of the
    APWorld (`rules.RuleCompiler(player, tricks)`, `regions.create_regions(world, tricks)`), never taken from
    `game.SETTINGS` (that only records the preset: all 0). Default: every trick off. See "Tricks" below.
  - `damage`: see `game.SETTINGS["damage"]`.
  - `misc`/`version`: static switches from `game.SETTINGS` (`misc_resources`, `version_resources`); `negate` means "value < amount".
- `{"type": "node", "node": ...}` does not occur at present.

**Not supported:** `item` with `negate` ("no item", 0×) and `node` (0×) count as not satisfied.
`event` with `negate: True` ("before event X", 54×, 22 events, not monotonic) counts as **satisfied** in the logic (E18);
the node lock catches the trap behind it. All of them stay in the data.

**Node lock (E18).** Dangerous is every event that occurs negated somewhere (derived from the data, 22).
In the game, merely entering its event node already triggers the event; afterwards "before X" is false and some paths are closed.
`escape_requirement` is the condition under which one gets from the event node in the state "after X" ("before X" = not satisfied,
event X = satisfied) to a ship (node of type `teleporter_network` whose `is_unlocked` holds), using only the
items one has on entering. The converter attaches it with AND to **every** connection into the event node. The APWorld
evaluates the data as usual and needs **no special logic**.
- Form: OR of minimal AND terms, leaves only `item`, `damage` and `event` (without `negate`).
  `{"and": []}` = always satisfied, `{"or": []}` = never. Starting items are item leaves like all others (E23).
- Computed without tricks (E23); `misc` and `version` are fixed with the preset values. With tricks the lock is
  therefore stricter than necessary, never too loose (it sits on every connection into the node, trick connections
  included).
- Other "before Y" count as satisfied on the way back (as everywhere in the logic).
- **Cycle-free:** events that are not reachable with all items without X (`escape_inlined_events`) are not a
  leaf in the tree, but are replaced by their own requirement from the event node, recursively (e.g. Gandrayda:
  "Proving Grounds Barrier Removed"). All other events stay `event` leaves.
- Control values (test; without tricks, node entered with minimal items): Gateway Green Lock → Grapple Lasso missing,
  Imperial Crypt Ice Floor → Screw Attack, Xenoresearch Power Outage → Seeker Missile, Gandrayda → Grapple Voltage,
  Flux Control Tunnel Cover → Spider Ball or X-Ray Visor. Aurora Chamber Vaccine and Spire Bomb: no trap.
- With all items, without tricks and with the lock, the goal, all 99 locations and 21 of the 22 dangerous events are reachable.
  "Gel Processing Site Out of Bounds" only works via trick (even without the lock); with all tricks it is all 22.
- If the player triggers an event too early against the logic, reloading helps (E18; whether that works in the game: T21).

**Dead-end locations (E22, T25, T30).** Some pickups can be reached but not left without a certain item (T08 B5: the
Bryyo Leviathan Core after Mogenar is left only with Hyper Ball). The converter computes an `escape_requirement`
for **every** pickup node with the same solver as the node lock: the way from the pickup node to a ship in the state
"after the pickup and after all events on the way there". It is stored in `LOCATIONS` and is the location's access
rule; the APWorld compiles it like any requirement (no special logic).
- State: `escape_triggered_events` = the events that every way to the node **without tricks** triggers (the node is
  unreachable with all items when the event, and for a database event its node, is blocked): "before X" is false
  for them. `escape_assumed_events` = the part that every way even **with every trick** (TRICK_COVERAGE) triggers:
  they count as reached. The others stay event leaves, because a trick may skip them on the way in (34 locations
  have such events). Other "before Y" count as satisfied, as everywhere.
- Cycle-free: events that are only reachable through the pickup node (`escape_inlined_events`) are replaced by their
  own requirement from there. Connections already carry the node lock, so a way out through a dangerous event node
  needs that node's escape too.
- Leaves: `item`, `damage`, `event` (no `negate`). **Starting items are item leaves** (T30; before, they counted as
  owned and never appeared). Computed **without tricks**; `misc`/`version` fixed with the preset values.
- **Trivial** (stored as `{"and": []}`): every state that reaches the pickup node satisfies it, for **every starting
  inventory and every trick setting** up to TRICK_COVERAGE (all 18 tricks at level 5). Checked exactly: the forward
  DNF from the start with every trick enabled, all events inlined and no starting items gives the minimal item sets
  that reach the node; for each of them the requirement must hold with the events that set reaches without tricks
  (the fewest any setting reaches; the logic is monotonic in items, tricks and events). 28 locations are trivial
  and 71 have a rule. Location 91 is the addition in T36.
- With the default starting items and no tricks, 23 location rules restrict access beyond reaching the node
  (exact test `test_default_setup_location_rules`). These are the 22 T25 rules and Flux Control re-entry at 91.
- Why the 48 extra rules are needed (test `test_location_rules_hold_for_every_setup`, before T30 it failed): without
  Morph Ball Bombs, 15 (Valhalla MedLab Alpha), 55, 79, 80 and 81 could be entered but not left; with tricks, 17, 67,
  77, 83, 87 and 90 (and more) could be reached by a trick without the items for the way back. Control value: with
  every item but Morph Ball Bombs, location 15 is the only location whose node is reachable while its rule fails.
- The item placed at a location is not known to the rule (the pickup's own item never counts). So a location whose
  escape needs its own vanilla item cannot hold that item any more (accepted in E22): 63 Boost Ball,
  64 Spider Ball, 76 Hazard Shield, 95 Nova Beam (Progressive Beam), 97 Hyper Missile, 98 Hyper Ball, 99 Hyper Grapple.
- Control values (test, from `randovania/games/prime3/logic_database/* - Seed.txt`): 98 Bryyo Leviathan Core =
  Hyper Ball + Hypermode (HyperModeTank, Energy Tank) + Morph Ball; 97 Elysian Leviathan Core = Hyper Missile +
  Missile ≥ 4; 99 Pirate Homeworld Leviathan Core = Hyper Grapple + Grapple Voltage + Grapple Lasso. The cores are
  reachable without these items, only the locations are not.

Location 84 is reachable with the default starting items alone (all landing sites are unlocked in this preset), but
it is only left with Boost Ball or Spider Ball. Events in the requirements are reached on the way out or elsewhere;
the AP state holds them as event items.

**Playthrough simulator** (`apworld/tools/playthrough_sim.py`, only on this data): random fill in the AP manner
(progression one at a time onto locations reachable with all remaining progression items whose
`escape_requirement` holds, then filler) and a player who follows the logic. They only enter a dangerous event node
if its escape and re-entry requirements hold. The event triggers, they then stand at the node and only get further via real
paths ("before X" false, connections without lock). They only enter a location if its `escape_requirement` holds
(dead-end rule); collecting it means walking to the pickup node, and if they cannot walk back from there to where
they stood (physically, with the item), they now stand at the pickup node. `trapped` = no ship reachable from where
they end.
`World.reach(..., logic=True)` = AP logic, `logic=False` = game physics, `gated=False` = logic without lock,
`World(data, location_escapes=False)` = logic without the location rules (before E22).
Test (seeds 0–99, allowed events half the time even before collecting): 100/100 won, all 99 locations each time,
never trapped. Control tests: without the lock the same player gets stuck; without the location rules (fill and
player) 2/100 seeds are won and 98/100 end trapped (mostly in location 84); without only location 98's rule the
player is stranded in the Bryyo Leviathan Core in 7/100 seeds (B5), without only 99's in 18/100.

### `game.py`

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `VICTORY_REQUIREMENT` | victory condition, a requirement: event `Aurora Unit 313` |
| `START_LOCATION` | starting node `(region, area, node)` = Valhalla, Docking Bay 5, Samus Ship |
| `SETTINGS` | preset settings that affect the logic (below) |
| `TRICKS` | `{trick name: {"short_name"}}`, 18 tricks |
| `TRICK_LEVEL_NAMES` | `{0: "disabled", … 5: "hypermode"}` |
| `REQUIREMENT_KINDS` | count of all requirement kinds in the tree (control) |
| `UNSUPPORTED_KINDS` | kinds that cannot be evaluated, with `count` and reason |

`SETTINGS`:
- `trick_level`: `minimal_logic` (off), `default_level`, `levels` = `{trick name: level}` (all 0). Preset information
  only: neither the converter nor the APWorld reads the trick levels from here (E23).
- `damage`: `strictness` 1.5, `starting_energy` 99, `energy_per_tank` 100, `reductions` = `{damage type: [(item or None, factor)]}` (currently empty).
  A `damage` requirement with amount `a` is satisfied if `99 + 100 × Energy Tanks > ceil(reduction × int(a × strictness))`
  (reduction = smallest factor of the items owned, otherwise 1.0). Randovania computes damage along the path with heal nodes
  (`heal`); that cannot be reproduced in AP. The approximation (full energy per requirement) is optimistic.
- `misc_resources`: `Skipping Energy Cells`, `Entrance Randomizer`, `Phaaze Skip`, `MP3Update` (all 0). `version_resources`: only `NTSC` = 1.
- `other`: `teleporters`, `skip_final_bosses`, `dock_rando` (vanilla), `available_locations` (full), `start_with_corrupted_hypermode`, `MP3Update`, `disable_deflicker` (for information only).

### `tricks.py` (T30)

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `TRICK_COVERAGE` | `{trick name: 5}` for all 18 tricks: the trick setting the location rules are safe for (any setting up to it) |
| `USABLE_MAX_LEVEL` | 3 (advanced): highest level the recommendation offers (E23 "off … advanced") |
| `USABLE_TRICKS` | **recommendation for T31**: `{trick name: highest offered level}` (table below) |
| `TRICK_REPORT` | per trick: `short_name`, `uses` (trick leaves per level, templates once), `requirements` (connections/event sources asking for it per level, templates expanded), `rooms`, `with_before`/`with_damage`/`with_unsupported` (AND terms that combine it with "before <event>", damage or an unsupported kind), per level `earlier_locations`/`earlier_events`/`new_events`, `usable_level`, `reason` |
| `COMBINED_REPORT` | the same gains for all `USABLE_TRICKS` together (`usable`) and for `TRICK_COVERAGE` (`coverage`) |

"Earlier" = with the trick alone at that level (all others off) the AP access (node reachable and
`escape_requirement`) needs fewer items in some case than without tricks (minimal item sets compared exactly; no
starting items assumed). `new_events` = reachable only with the trick, even with every item.

## Tricks (E23, T30)

**Interface for the APWorld.** A trick leaf `{"type": "trick", "name": t, "amount": L}` is satisfied when the slot's
level for `t` is at least `L` (levels 0–5, `game.TRICK_LEVEL_NAMES`). The APWorld passes the slot's levels as a dict
`{trick name: level}`: `regions.create_regions(world, tricks)` builds the regions with
`rules.RuleCompiler(player, tricks)` and prunes with `regions.reachable_graph(tricks)` (nodes and events reachable
with every item and these tricks). Missing tricks are off; unknown names or levels outside 0–5 raise `ValueError`.
Without the argument (as `__init__.py` calls it today) every trick is off, so the default options behave as before
T30. T31 should offer only `USABLE_TRICKS`, each up to its level, marked experimental.

**Safety.** Escape requirements are computed without tricks; the node lock sits on every connection into a dangerous
event node, trick connections included; location rules are stored wherever a trick (up to `TRICK_COVERAGE`) could
lead into a location without the items for the way back. So any trick setting is safe in the sense of E18/E22, only
stricter than necessary: with tricks, a way out that needs a trick is not counted. The logic with tricks is never
weaker than without (every rule holds wherever the no-trick logic reaches the location).

**Criteria for `USABLE_TRICKS`** (`convert_db.py`): highest level ≤ 3 at which the trick is asked for by at least 3
requirements and makes at least one location reachable earlier; never combined with an unsupported kind ("no item",
node); not excluded by hand: *Single Room Out of Bounds* (leaves the level geometry, the dangerous event Gel Processing
Site Out of Bounds exists only through it), *Fall Respawn Skip* (respawn not modelled), *Hazards without Hazard
Shield* (hazard routes on damage requirements; the AP damage rule checks each with full energy). The simulator
checks the result ("Check matrix").

| Standable Terrain | 1: 10/9, 2: 4/4 | 7 | 0 at every level | 0 | 2 / 1 | no (no location earlier) |
| Terminal Fall Abuse | 1: 7/7, 2: 2/2, 3: 2/2 | 8 | 1: 2, 2: 2, 3: 2 | 1: 9 … 3: 9 | 1 / 0 | **3 (advanced)** |
| Single Room Out of Bounds | 2: 2/2, 3: 11/11, 4: 1/1, 5: 4/4 | 8 | 2: 0, 3: 0, 4: 4, 5: 4 | 2: 1 … 5: 10 | 2 / 0 | no (excluded) |
| Open Barriers from Behind | 1: 4/4, 2: 2/2 | 5 | 1: 0, 2: 8 | 1: 0, 2: 7 | 0 / 0 | **2 (intermediate)** |
| Screw Attack at Z-Axis | 2: 1/1, 3: 1/1 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 | no (too few uses) |
| Fall Respawn Skip | 3: 9/9, 4: 9/9, 5: 3/3 | 5 | 0 at every level | 0 | 0 / 0 | no (excluded) |
| Hazards without Hazard Shield | 1: 9/9, 2: 4/4, 3: 5/5, 4: 6/5 | 10 | 1: 0, 2: 7, 3: 7, 4: 8 | 1: 0 … 4: 35 | 4 / 39 | no (excluded) |
| Combat | 1: 11/10, 2: 16/13, 3: 11/8, 4: 9/7, 5: 1/1 | 15 | 1: 18, 2: 19, 3: 19, 4: 19, 5: 19 | 1: 36 … 5: 40 | 13 / 126 | **3 (advanced)** |

`USABLE_TRICKS` = Bomb Jump 3, Slope Jump 3, Knowledge 3, Movement 3, Bomb/Spring Space Jump 3, Invisible Objects 2,
Terminal Fall Abuse 3, Open Barriers from Behind 2, Combat 3. Together they make 72 of the 99 locations and 128
database events reachable earlier (no new event); all 18 at level 5 make 74 locations earlier and add the dangerous
event Gel Processing Site Out of Bounds (needs Single Room Out of Bounds + Bomb Jump, T20). The per-trick location
lists are in `TRICK_REPORT[...]["earlier_locations"]`. Knowledge and Combat lean on damage requirements (36/126 AND
terms): the optimistic damage rule above applies to them as to all damage leaves.

## Missable locations and re-entry (E24, T36)

The in-game intro starts on G.F.S. Olympus. The graph starts at `G.F.S. Valhalla / Docking Bay 5 / Samus Ship`.
From there the default teleporter network reaches `Olympus / Gunship / Samus Ship`, but the outgoing area edge
`Samus Ship → Dock to Docking Bay 5` requires `Aurora Unit 313`, the victory event in the Phaaze sanctum. With that
event blocked, all items and all 18 tricks at level 5 reach exactly 97 AP pickup nodes. The missing two are:

| ID | G.F.S. Olympus pickup | Edges and events |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ventilation Shaft, Energy Tank | Behind the Gunship gate. The shaft edge `Morph Ball Door to Xenoresearch Lab → Pickup (Energy Tank)` needs Morph Ball + Morph Ball Bomb. The pickup can lead on toward Disposal Chamber, which has a dock to Repair Bay A. |
| 2 | Munitions Storage, Missile Launcher | Behind the same Gunship gate. The room's edge `Door to Repair Bay A → Pickup (Missile Launcher)` has no requirement. Server-granted Missiles can satisfy the intro's missile requirements without collecting this pickup. In the reported seed, leaving it unchecked cost the player Hazard Shield. |

The other cross-region route leaves Docking Bay 5 via `Event - Berserker Lord → Dock to Tower Elevator`.
The approach to that boss requires `Ready Room Briefing`. On Norion, the return through Cargo Hub is blocked by
`Door from Tower Elevator → Tower Elevator / Door to Cargo Hub` (impossible requirement). Tower Elevator can
lead to Control Tower, where `Event - Activate Cannon` (`Norion Defense Cannon`) leads to `Dock to MedLab Delta`
on Olympus. This route therefore does not give an independent entrance from the later Norion landing sites.
The MedLab Delta PED (pickup index 0) is local to the game. E13/E17 leave it unpatched and outside the 99 AP checks.

For each of the 22 events used in a "before X" requirement, the converter compares the reachable targets of those
edges before and after X. It credits events that every exit to a ship triggers, tested by blocking each candidate
with all items and tricks. All 99 AP pickup nodes remain reachable after each event with that inventory and trick
coverage. Some nodes, including the pre-bomb Spire Dock entrances, disappear without taking a pickup node with them.
Two places cost more to reach again with tricks off:

| Event | Edge affected after the event | Generated rule |
|---|---|---|
| Aurora Chamber (Elysia) Vaccine | In Main Docking Bay, `Samus Ship (Catch.) ⇄ Door to Main Docking Access` needs Plasma Beam + Ghor. The ship reaches `Before Ghor` after Vaccine, and `Before Ghor → Event - Ghor` needs Enter Hypermode with tricks off. Before T36, the logic could still expect checks 53–65 after the player left and came back, even without the items to get back in. | AND Energy Tank + HyperModeTank + Plasma Beam into every edge entering the Vaccine event, alongside the escape gate. |
| Flux Control Tunnel Cover | `Lower Level → Pickup (Missile Expansion)` in Flux Control needs Grapple Lasso once the `before Flux Control Tunnel Cover` alternative closes. The pickup is location 91. | AND the post-event path into 91's location rule. With tricks off, the nodes beyond the pickup do not get more expensive to reach. The event itself keeps its E18 escape gate. |

After `Xenoresearch Power Outage`, blocking either `Xenoresearch A Seeker Gate` or
`Xenoresearch B Seeker Gate` prevents reaching a ship from the event node, even with all items and tricks.
Both are recorded in `reentry_assumed_events`, so the return path can use them. The checks in Xenoresearch A
and B (69 and 70) remain accessible with the items needed in the default logic.

The generated event records list changed targets under `reentry_endpoints`: `gated` for the Vaccine,
`location` for 91, `lost` for unreachable non-pickup nodes, and `tricks_only` for extra costs exposed by
the level-5 trick comparison alone. The last group is diagnostic and has no additional gate. The two re-entry
rules use no tricks and assume no starting items.

The APWorld marks both locations `EXCLUDED` during region creation (T38). Archipelago's early-item and main fills
honor that classification, and the opening chain in [`opening.py`](../opening.py) skips excluded checks.
The client warns while the player is on Olympus if either check is still open.

## Check matrix (T30, T36)

`playthrough_sim.py --matrix` runs the fill and a logic-following player for seeds 0–99, triggering eligible events
early half the time (`eager` 0.5). The test `test_check_matrix` runs seeds 0–39, or 0–19 with the minimal start.
Removed starting items go into the pool, one Missile Expansion leaves it per item. Sphere 0 is what the logic
allows with the starting items alone.

| Setup | Sphere 0 | Fill failed | Won, 99/99 | Trapped | Not won |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 3 (4, 11, 17) | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |
| without Morph Ball | 2 (4, 11) | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |
| without Morph Ball Bombs | 2 | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |
| without Space Jump Boots | 2 | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |
| without Charge Beam | 2 | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |
| only Power Beam + Combat/Scan Visor | 2 | **73/100** | 27/27 filled | 0 | – |
| usable tricks at the recommended level | 4 | 0 | 100/100 | 0 | – |

With `eager` 0 (events only when nothing else is left) the counts are the same in every row.

All 627 filled seeds won with 99/99 checks. The four Vaccine re-entry failures in the T30 matrix are gone (seeds
40 without Space Jump Boots, 72 without Charge Beam, 34 and 59 with recommended tricks). T30 also recorded five
Vaccine failures in default seeds 100–499. The minimum starting setup still leaves only two initial checks for
the simulator's fill. The re-entry rules change the legal placements, so its 20-attempt budget succeeds on 27
seeds where the old data succeeded on 25. Fill failures occur before play and are counted separately.

**Starting items (T31).** Sphere 0 is never empty: for all 16 choices of the removable starting items (Charge
Beam, Space Jump Boots, Morph Ball, Morph Ball Bombs) it holds locations 4 and 11 (`--start-table`), so every setup
can start. The additional combinations below are the historical T30 measurements (20 attempts per seed, seeds 0–99).

| Removed | Fill failed |
|---|---|
| none, any one item, or any two items | 0 (Space Jump Boots + Morph Ball: 1; Space Jump Boots + Bombs: 3; Morph Ball + Bombs: 3) |
| Charge Beam + Space Jump Boots + Bombs | 3 |
| Charge Beam + Morph Ball + Bombs | 12 |
| Charge Beam + Space Jump Boots + Morph Ball | 14 |
| Space Jump Boots + Morph Ball + Bombs | 65 |
| all four (only Power Beam + Combat/Scan Visor) | 75 |

The figures above describe the simulator. Archipelago uses T29's local early Screw Attack with the default options.
For reduced starting inventories, [`opening.py`](../opening.py) (T31) places a short forward chain of local
progression items before the main fill. [`test_generation.py`](../test/test_generation.py) exercises the actual
Archipelago fill for all 16 starting-item combinations and verifies filler on both Olympus checks.

## Use by the APWorld (T04, T30)

1. One AP location per `LOCATIONS` entry (ID = `id`), in the room `(region, area)`, access rule = its
   `escape_requirement` (E22). Locations with `missable: "after_goal"` are `EXCLUDED` (E24, T38).
2. `count` items per `ITEMS` entry. `progression` controls the AP class.
3. Location 0 (`UNPATCHED_LOCATION`) is not a location and does not occur in the logic. Hypermode is a normal pool item.
4. Translate requirement trees into rules: "before event" = satisfied, "no item" and `node` = not satisfied.
   The node lock is already in `CONNECTIONS` (`escape_gate` for information only).
5. Tricks: the slot's levels as a parameter (`create_regions(world, tricks)`), only `USABLE_TRICKS` (above).
6. Starting items (E23, T31): any subset of `STARTING_ITEMS` that keeps Power Beam, Combat Visor and Scan Visor; the
   removed ones go into the pool and Missile Expansions leave it. [`opening.py`](../opening.py) (T31) gives reduced
   inventories a forward progression chain before the main fill. See "Check matrix" for the generation tests.
